what_its_for: Doxepin is used to treat depression, anxiety, and trouble sleeping (insomnia). A skin cream form is also available to relieve itching caused by certain skin conditions. Your doctor chose this medicine to help improve your mood, reduce worry, or help you get a better night's sleep.
how_to_take: Take doxepin exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take the capsule or liquid form with or without food. If you are taking it for sleep, take it within 30 minutes of going to bed. Do not crush or chew the capsules — swallow them whole. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided. Mix the liquid with 4 ounces (half a cup) of water, milk, or juice — do NOT mix it with carbonated drinks (like soda). For the skin cream, apply a thin layer only to the itchy area and gently rub it in.
dosing: The dose of doxepin is different for each person and depends on what it is being used for. For depression or anxiety, doses typically range from 75 mg to 300 mg per day, taken as one dose at bedtime or split into smaller doses during the day. For sleep problems, the dose is much lower — usually 3 mg to 6 mg taken once at bedtime. For the skin cream, apply a thin coat 3 to 4 times a day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are taking doxepin only at bedtime for sleep and you do not remember until morning, skip that dose entirely.
storage: Store doxepin capsules and liquid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid tightly closed. Store the skin cream at room temperature and do not freeze it. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking doxepin — it can make drowsiness much worse and increase your risk of side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as doxepin can cause dizziness. Do not take other sleep aids, anxiety medicines, pain medicines, or antihistamines (like Benadryl) without asking your doctor first. If you use the skin cream, avoid covering the treated area with a tight bandage and keep it away from your eyes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you or someone you know experiences: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, unusual changes in mood or behavior, severe confusion, a fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty urinating, severe dizziness or fainting, seizures, or signs of an allergic reaction (rash, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing). Also call your doctor if you feel more depressed, very agitated, or have new or worsening anxiety. In the US, contact the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline by calling or texting 988 if you are in crisis.
when_it_works: For depression and anxiety, doxepin may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start to feel better, and it may take up to 6 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you do not feel better right away — give it time. For sleep problems, doxepin may work the very first night you take it. For the skin cream, itching relief usually begins within a few days of use. Keep taking your medicine as directed even if you feel well, and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Doxepin causes more dizziness and drowsiness in older people, which raises the fall and injury risk. Older adults are often started on a much lower dose. This medicine is on the Beers List of medicines that should be used with caution in older adults. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking doxepin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It may harm the unborn baby. Breastfeeding: Doxepin passes into breast milk and can cause serious side effects in a nursing baby, including excessive sleepiness. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Doxepin is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age. Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts in children and teenagers — watch closely for changes in mood or behavior and contact the doctor immediately if you notice any.
